title.narrative: Contributing to conflict transformation and social cohesion among displaced, demobilized returnees

description.narrative:
The project seeks to address the issue of social cohesion between displaced, demobilized, returnees and residents in the hills around Bujumbura in Burundi. These groups were separated during the war that Burundi faced during 1993 and were people were killed on ethnic basis. The 2015 recent elections were held in a tense environment and regional and African initiatives are underway to require dialogue between those in power and the other major players in the Burundi crisis to prevent the country from slipping further into the war. Through proposed project’ activities, people living in IDP camps, returnees, demobilized and residents will have a framework of encounter and exchange in order to dispel mistrust. Each week, these people will hold meetings where they will discuss peace and coexistence. Project plans to implement 27 SILCs (Saving and Internal Lending Communities) consisting of 20 people each living together in the hills. CDJP will not fund the SILCs’ capital start up. The initial capital will be granted by contributions from SILCs members. The project is planning to grant small premiums for field officers who will be responsible for the supervision of these SILCS. One Internal Micro credit expert will support SILCs management. SILCs members will set a credit union that will be fuelled by contributions from members. After making contributions, they will proceed to the distribution of small credits to those who need them at an agreed interest rate in the group. SILC’s meeting planned will also be an opportunity to discuss the challenges of cohabitation in the hills and therefore an opportunity to resolve disputes. Project aims to focus on these common economic interests for beneficiaries that will promote collaboration, understanding, peaceful coexistence and even reconciliation. By implementing this current project, changes that CDJP Bujumbura intends to contribute to are : • The conflicts are managed and processed peacefully within beneficiaries • The social and political injustices are reduced in communities targeted • Solidarity is consolidated between the war displaced, demobilized, repatriated and hills residents around Bujumbura • To gradually increase economic independence of SILCs members that will allow them to resist to political manipulation • Project’s beneficiaries behaviours and attitudes changes that are reflected in their living environment by their support to the reconciliation and peaceful coexistence among them • Income levels and living conditions of displaced people, demobilized, residents and returnees is improved and thus they can withstand the various political manipulation.
The activities under this project will be executed in three parishes (Rushubi, Munanira and Kivoga) in the Archdiocese of Bujumbura.
